speaker: The Minister for Manpower and Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Mr Chairman, I thank the Members who have spoken.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower and Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: In my response, I will provide an update of our population strategies and measures to support Marriage and Parenthood.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower and Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Dr Lim Wee Kiak asked how we will build a sustainable and vibrant Singapore for all ages in light of our demographic challenges.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower and Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: We are doing so through three broad strategies.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower and Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Our first and foremost strategy in managing the population is to ensure that there is always a new generation of Singaporeans to carry our legacy forward.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower and Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: We want Singapore to be a Great Place for Families, where young couples sense the strong support for marriage and parenthood from society and the state.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower and Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: In addressing this question, it is useful to take a step back.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower and Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: When we consider developments over longer time periods, there are some reasons to be optimistic.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower and Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: From 2009 to 2013, the average was lower at 31,400 citizen births annually.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower and Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: If we go back to an even earlier period, between 2004 and 2008, the annual average was 32,000 births.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower and Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: So, for the most recent five-year period, we are talking about 33,000 citizen births on average annually.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower and Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: The five years before that, it was 31,400; and the five years before that, it was 32,000.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower and Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: This average is also higher than that of the previous five-year periods.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower and Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: From 2009 to 2013, there was an average of about 1,400 overseas citizen births annually.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower and Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: And between 2004 and 2008, this average was 1,000 overseas citizen births.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower and Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: In fact, the average number of marriages in the past five years was significantly higher than the past decade.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower and Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Juxtaposed against these developments is another set of forces at play.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower and Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Most young Singaporeans still want to marry and have children, which Mr Vikram Nair would be glad to know.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower and Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: However, they are also taking longer to find the right partner and starting families later.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower and Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: But, given the positive marriage trends, I remain hopeful that there could be an uptick in TFR when the children of the Baby Boomers start having babies themselves.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower and Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: For family to remain the bedrock of society, which Mr Alex Yam spoke passionately about, we must actively lean against the wind to make marriage and parenthood achievable, enjoyable and celebrated.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower and Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: There are still many things in Singapore that are favourable to child-raising.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower and Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Last year, Singapore was ranked first in the World Bank's inaugural Human Capital Index.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower and Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: And what that means is that as far as the World Bank is concerned, for a child born in any of the 157 countries that they surveyed, Singapore would be where their human capital potential is most likely to be optimised.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower and Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: In the same year, an international non-governmental organisation, "Save The Children", also ranked Singapore as the best country for children to grow up in.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower and Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: The Government has also progressively enhanced our Marriage and Parenthood Package.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower and Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Mr Gan Thiam Poh and Mr Desmond Choo had asked about the progress and adequacy of our current measures.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower and Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Mr Chairman, Sir, may I have your permission to distribute a table showing the key marriage and parenthood benefits that a young couple can receive today, compared to five years ago?

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Mr Chairman, firstly, a couple can now own their first home sooner.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: First-timers buying a new flat in non-mature estates can service their housing loans using less than a quarter of their combined monthly incomes, often with little or no cash because they draw on their CPF savings instead.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Second, parents now benefit from greater support for child-raising costs.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: This is $3,000 more than the maximum a couple would get in 2014.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: They will also receive a CDA First Step of $3,000 deposited by the Government, without having to save into the CDA first, which helps to lighten their load at the start of their parenthood journey.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Third, in their child's preschool years, the couple would find it easier to enrol their child in an affordable and good quality preschool.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: The Early Childhood Development Agency (ECDA) has increased the number of full-day preschool places nationwide by over 50% since 2014.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: By 2023, this will increase to about 200,000, and two-thirds of preschoolers will be enrolled in Government-supported preschools.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Fourth, throughout their parenthood journey and as their family commitments increase, the couple now has stronger support to manage their work and family responsibilities today.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: They enjoy enhanced parental leave provisions, which enable fathers to play a more active role.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: We have also increased paid childcare leave over the years.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Today, each parent with children below age seven has six days of childcare leave per year, and two days of childcare leave per year while their children are still in primary school.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Mr Louis Ng gave suggestions on further increasing leave for parents to care for their children, while Mr Desmond Choo suggested legislating FWAs.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: We will keep reviewing the scope to expand leave provisions but, as Mr Douglas Foo reminded us, we should be careful about mandating businesses to do more as it would impact business viability and put jobs at risk.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Given the recent enhancements, I hope Members will agree to give companies some time to adjust before further moves.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: That is why we introduced a Tripartite Standard last year to encourage employers to provide unpaid leave when their employees have unexpected care needs, including multiple or preterm births, or family members or children who are hospitalised.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: I must thank Mr Louis Ng for giving us the idea.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: About 450 employers with over 224,000 staff combined, have adopted this Standard.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: This includes the Public Service with over 70 agencies.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: We will continue to encourage adoption of the Standard.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: I should also add that parents would be more likely to benefit from FWAs.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: We introduced the Tripartite Standard on FWAs in October 2017, and also launched the enhanced Work-Life Grant last July, to better support the adoption of FWAs.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: The grant has received more than 340 applications in just five months.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Around 53% of employers now offer at least one formal FWA.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: This could be flexi-time, flexi-place, flexi-load, and this is up from 47% in 2014.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: This is, in fact, a significant turning point I have been waiting for.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: The tide is shifting and I am hopeful FWAs will become much more commonplace henceforth.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Nevertheless, I am aware that young Singaporeans still have concerns, which Mr Desmond Choo also raised.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Parents have raised concerns about financial costs, such as preschool fees.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: ECDA is reviewing the preschool subsidy framework, to make quality preschool more affordable for parents.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: The Ministry for Social and Family Development (MSF) will provide an update on this during its COS debate.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Parents may also feel the need to keep up with other parents’ intensive efforts in education, for example.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: To help our students discover more joy and develop stronger intrinsic motivation to learn, MOE is reducing the frequency and stakes of school-based assessments.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Students' class and level positions will not be reflected in report books to minimise unhealthy comparisons among students based on their academic performance.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: MSF has also started the Baby Bonus Parenting Resources Portal to boost confidence in parenting through sharing of tips by experts on raising happy and healthy children.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Next, as Ms Rahayu Mahzam pointed out, the workplace environment is critical.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Senior Parliamentary Secretary Low Yen Ling will share more at MOM's COS debate.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: But overall, I am encouraged that more companies are taking progressive steps to support their employees' caregiving needs.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: One such example is M Tech, a small and medium enterprise (SME) which specialises in cybersecurity and network performance solutions.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: As many of their employees are young parents who may also be caring for elders in the family, M Tech decided to offer FWAs to staff who need them.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: This was made possible by IT tools which enable staff to work remotely and still be effective.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: I met Petrine, a product manager who was able to telecommute when her children were down with chickenpox, and when her mother was hospitalised.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: M Tech was initially concerned about the investment needed to enable mobile working but later found that the benefits were well worth it.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: For example, it is better able to attract and retain employees who are productive and committed to their work, such as Petrine, who has been with M Tech for 11 years.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Beyond workplace flexibility, there are deeper issues of workplace culture.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Some Singaporeans, indeed, work very long hours, leaving little time for dating or family life.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Having fewer hours to rest and recharge not only affects employees' health and well-being, but also the time that they have with their loved ones.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: As the nature of work evolves, there is value for organisations to adopt new ways of working that achieve good business outcomes while giving staff enough downtime to recharge.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: M Tech employees, for example, may get off work early, whether to attend courses or to pick up their children from childcare.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: But they would reconnect later in the evening to complete time-sensitive tasks, such as confirming sales orders taken in other time zones, and they do not mind doing it at all because it does not take very long.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: So, we hope many more employers will make the effort to promote more sustainable work practices, for the sake of their employees and for their own business viability in the longer run.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Members, including Mr Ong Teng Koon, Mr Saktiandi Supaat and Mr Vikram Nair, have given suggestions on further measures to strengthen support for marriage and parenthood.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: However, porting over practices in other countries wholesale may not yield the desired results.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: I think for South Korea, this is the lowest they have on record.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Our efforts over the last five years are significant, even if they may take more time to bear fruit.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: We also need deeper changes of mindsets to reduce stresses in parenting.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Ultimately, marriage and parenthood are personal decisions, shaped by the values that each person holds dear, but they are also influenced in no small part by social norms, our families, employers and the wider society.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: There are strong cultural and societal factors at play.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Like Mr Saktiandi Supaat and Mr Alex Yam have pointed out, no single stakeholder can fully address these on its own.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: In this regard, I am encouraged to see how various community stakeholders have stepped up.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: The Families for Life Council, for example, offers a suite of education programmes at workplaces and community touchpoints.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: It also organises events to encourage Singaporeans to make family life a priority.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: In Boon Lay Constituency, a Parents' Support Group was formed after a group of young parents met at the PA's Embracing PArenthood community celebrations.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: The group meets quarterly to share tips about child development, infant nutrition, and other parenting pointers.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Such efforts, big or small, go a long way in making parenthood enjoyable and celebrated.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: I also appreciate the Members' suggestions and there are many good examples.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: So, I would like to invite all stakeholders to join us in co-creating and shaping policies.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: We will give more details about the consultation process soon.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Mr Chairman, I have taken some time to reaffirm our commitment to supporting marriage and parenthood.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Our second strategy in managing the population is to maintain a careful balance in immigrant flows.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: At its heart, the aim of our immigration policy is to sustain a stable citizen population that keeps our economy vibrant and our society cohesive.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: As Dr Lim Wee Kiak and Mr Gan Thiam Poh mentioned, it is important that citizens share a strong sense of identity and belonging to Singapore.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: We also agree with Prof Fatimah Lateef that it matters how we select new citizens.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: To this end, we conduct regular reviews of our immigration framework.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: We remain highly selective in granting permanent residencies and citizenships.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: In all cases, we consider the applicants' age, family profile, economic contributions, as well as their ability to integrate, among other factors.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: We look for markers of rootedness and identification with Singapore's way of life, values and norms.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Family ties and length of stay provide a strong indication of this.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: We will continue to maintain a careful balance in managing immigration.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Mr Chairman, our third and equally important strategy in building a sustainable population is to enable Singaporeans to age with grace and purpose.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: The United Nations (UN) has described population ageing as one of the defining features of our time.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: In Asia, Japan was the first country to age rapidly.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Singapore, together with South Korea, Hong Kong and Taiwan, is not far behind.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Fortunately, more of these years are enjoyed in good health than before.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Far from being resigned to this development, our approach is to help Singaporeans enjoy productive longevity, in many varied ways.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: It starts with being able to stay active, having the opportunity to work if seniors wish to, and strengthening support for retirement adequacy.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Since the 1980s, we have been putting in place measures to prepare for an ageing society.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Besides home ownership, it now helps Singaporeans save for healthcare needs and receive payouts for life in their retirement.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: This is in addition to regular top-ups to boost retirement savings.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: As the recent Parliamentary Motion on Ageing with Purpose affirmed, we should continue to improve our policies to support the changing profile of seniors.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: For example, more seniors wish to work longer.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Our employment rate of those aged 55 to 64 is already among the highest in the world and still going up.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: In my capacity as Manpower Minister, I set up a Tripartite Workgroup on Older Workers.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Later in the debate, I will provide an update on the Workgroup's deliberations that will address Mr Gan Thiam Poh's concerns about supporting senior employment.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Within our communities, we are also updating the way we care for seniors, for example, through innovative, award-winning solutions like Kampung Admiralty.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: My colleagues at the Ministry of Health (MOH) will share more during their COS debate.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: (In Mandarin):   Mr Chairman, we will continue to strengthen our efforts to make Singapore a Great Place for Families.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: We have significantly strengthened support for marriage and parenthood in recent years, for example, in the areas of housing, child-raising costs, preschool, and managing their work and family responsibilities.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Compared to even five years ago, young parents are much better supported.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: While the Government strengthens its support, we also need the whole of society to make Singapore a Great Place for Families.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: For example, employers and co-workers can help by accommodating parents’ needs for FWAs.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Community organisations can also celebrate parenthood and build networks of support among peers.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: We will embark on a consultation process in the coming months to listen to the needs and concerns of Singaporeans over forming families.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: We hope that various stakeholders will continue giving feedback and join us in making Singapore a truly Great Place for Families.

speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
text: That said, some of these initiatives seem to have been started as standalone programmes, with Government agencies and Statutory Boards launching their own initiatives.

speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Can the Prime Minister's Office elaborate more on the larger national narrative guiding the Smart Nation Initiative and how it has delivered tangible benefits to citizens and businesses?

speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Also, are there intentions to embark on a public-private partnership to commercialise current initiatives so that more benefits can be delivered to end users by private sector players?

speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
text: People must be at the heart of our Smart Nation efforts.

speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
text: Solution should deal with only modern problems to make urban living easier for our people.

speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
text: These could include transportation, energy efficiency, public safety, public health, citizen engagement, privacy and cybersecurity.

speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
text: We need to solicit citizens' and businesses' buy-in.

speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
text: Benefits have to be real for them to believe in it.

speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
text: Hence, designing solutions to be citizen- or user-centric is imperative.

speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
text: Secure digital identity (ID) also enables Estonians to complete transactions efficiently and securely.

speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
text: When a child is born, for example, the hospital enters the information in its database that is linked to the National Population Register.

speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
text: The information is shared automatically with various government systems that then ensure the child receives social benefits, such as healthcare and education.

speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
text: Given our aspirations and the experiences of other countries, how would the Government ensure that services are citizen-centric?

speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
text: While it is the Government's plan to make its services more data-driven and anticipatory, what more can citizens and businesses expect to benefit from our Smart Nation efforts?

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim
text: On 12 February this year, the Minister for Communications and Information told the House that GovTech is overall in charge of the security and safeguards systems for data and that Government Technology Agency (GovTech) is the agency that does many of the reviews, ensures the Government agencies are in compliance with the Instruction Manuals and other provisions.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim
text: For instance, does GovTech audit the data and privacy protection practices of public agencies?

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim
text: Next, while there are regulations to punish public officers who do not comply with confidentiality obligations, what is the position of the innocent persons whose data has been compromised?

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim
text: For instance, it was recently reported that a station inspector had illegally accessed the Police's computer system to screen the telephone records of a man he suspected of having an affair with his wife.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim
text: In such a case, are there guidelines about whether the affected person should be told and within a certain timeframe?

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim
text: Such information is crucial for victims to protect themselves and to seek recourse in a timely manner.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim
text: Besides commencing an expensive lawsuit against the Government, how else can an aggrieved person get compensation?

speaker: Mr Cedric Foo Chee Keng
text: Mr Chairman, my cut is on our Smart Nation vision and programmes.

speaker: Mr Cedric Foo Chee Keng
text: Our Smart Nation vision is a good one.

speaker: Mr Cedric Foo Chee Keng
text: A digital Government will allow for an integrated and seamless Government, resulting in better policies and operations.

speaker: Mr Cedric Foo Chee Keng
text: A digital economy will increase productivity for businesses, will create new jobs and opportunities right into the future.

speaker: Mr Cedric Foo Chee Keng
text: A digital society will allow our people to enjoy greater conveniences, increased opportunities and a higher quality of life.

speaker: Mr Cedric Foo Chee Keng
text: Since the inception of the Smart Nation initiative in late 2014, good progress has been made in applying digital and smart solutions to provide better services for our citizens and businesses.

speaker: Mr Cedric Foo Chee Keng
text: Several good programmes that have been introduced should be applauded.

speaker: Mr Cedric Foo Chee Keng
text: For preschoolers, parents can search for preschools, retrieve and view medical data of their child on the Moments of Life application.

speaker: Mr Cedric Foo Chee Keng
text: For many parents entering the exciting and busy journey of parenthood, the conveniences of a one-stop application versus a need to navigate various agencies and websites provide a real and tangible benefit.

speaker: Mr Cedric Foo Chee Keng
text: However, these initiatives are but a small step towards our Smart Nation goals.

speaker: Mr Cedric Foo Chee Keng
text: The technology curve has moved very rapidly and what was not possible is now possible.

speaker: Mr Cedric Foo Chee Keng
text: Chairman, my next cut is on preparing for the future.

speaker: Mr Cedric Foo Chee Keng
text: Despite lacking in traditional factors of production like land, labour and capital, Singapore was able to beat the odds in our transformation from a Third-World country to a First-World country today.

speaker: Mr Cedric Foo Chee Keng
text: Our success can be attributed to strong and honest leadership, a tolerant multiracial society and a culture of self-reliance and mutual support.

speaker: Mr Cedric Foo Chee Keng
text: Today, we face a fresh set of challenges – an ageing society, sharper infrastructure and manpower constraints, just to name a few.

speaker: Mr Cedric Foo Chee Keng
text: Amidst a global digital revolution, Singapore has to accelerate the transformation of our society and economy in order to remain competitive or risk being left behind.

speaker: Mr Cedric Foo Chee Keng
text: There are many benefits to a digital economy.

speaker: Mr Cedric Foo Chee Keng
text: Higher productivity, better quality of life, better jobs, reduced business operating costs and the list goes on.

speaker: Mr Cedric Foo Chee Keng
text: Because of the significant benefits to citizens and businesses, other cities and nations around the world are also embarking on similar digitalisation efforts.

speaker: Mr Cedric Foo Chee Keng
text: In October 2018, Emirates launched trials of the world's first biometric pathways at Dubai International Airport.

speaker: Mr Cedric Foo Chee Keng
text: This allows the use of biometric technology through Smart immigration tunnels, with passengers walking through immigration without a need to stop at a counter.

speaker: Mr Cedric Foo Chee Keng
text: As other countries embark on similar digitalisation efforts, what is the Government doing on the Smart Nation front to ensure that we remain relevant and globally competitive?

speaker: Mr Teo Ser Luck (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: We have shared our vision to become a Smart Nation and there have been announcements and programmes implemented.

speaker: Mr Teo Ser Luck (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: And through Smart Nation, there are many opportunities we can help to liven all the startups and also local businesses.

speaker: Mr Teo Ser Luck (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: So, may I know whether the Ministry or the Prime Minister's Office (PMO) could update on what is the impact on the businesses so far in terms of opportunities as well as in doing business within the Smart Nation project?

speaker: Mr Teo Ser Luck (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: There are many projects that the private sector has embarked on, especially the tech businesses.

speaker: Mr Teo Ser Luck (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: We should be able to tap on these startups or companies that develop these technologies, and especially when they have developed advanced state-of-the-art developments in AI, machine learning or automation.

speaker: Mr Teo Ser Luck (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: GovTech does not need to set up another group or another committee to redevelop or reinvent the wheel.

speaker: Mr Teo Ser Luck (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: It could partner these companies to go into a trial and test process.

speaker: Mr Teo Ser Luck (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: And many of these technologies have been tested by the market.

speaker: Mr Teo Ser Luck (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: Do consider them before setting up another major project within GovTech or within the Government.

speaker: Mr Teo Ser Luck (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: They can offer good help and better help.

speaker: Mr Teo Ser Luck (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: Could PMO update the business community what are the initiatives available through the Smart Nation project and what are the opportunities that will be available in future.

speaker: Mr Vikram Nair
text: Mr Chairman, the Singapore Government is leading the way in making Singapore a Smart Nation.

speaker: Mr Vikram Nair
text: GovTech is ensuring that more and more Government services are available online and are easy to use online.

speaker: Mr Vikram Nair
text: However, a Smart Nation may be led by a smart Government, but it will also need a "smart" private sector to take full advantage of the progress.

speaker: Mr Vikram Nair
text: In this respect, how is the Government involving the private sector and the tech community in this Smart Nation drive?

speaker: Mr Vikram Nair
text: What new initiatives can we expect in the coming year?

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: The Smart Nation effort is a commendable one.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: It is necessary to keep up with the changing global developments and ensure that our citizens can benefit from updated technology, so that we can all enjoy a better quality of life.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: Smart technology can also be used to make society more inclusive.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: Still, some have expressed concern that we may be changing too fast and that there are vulnerable groups in our community who may not be able to keep up with the change.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: Some are concerned that the elderly may not be digitally savvy and will have difficulties adjusting to the changes.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: I want to thank Mr Cedric Foo, Ms Tin Pei Ling, Mr Vikram Nair who have quite rightly emphasised that what matters is not technology for its own sake, but people, that is, what we do with the technology and how it benefits us in our daily lives.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: First, we have focused on increasing convenience in our daily lives.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: The MyInfo project allows you to open a bank account or apply for credit cards online and get approval almost instantly through carefully secured shared data.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: And, in fact, a lesser known fact that those of you who have linked your National Registration Identity Card (NRIC) number to PayNow can receive your SG Bonus, Edusave awards and, even more pertinent politically, can even receive your CPF lump-sum payments quickly, almost instantly, instead of waiting for cheques to arrive in the mail.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: I forgot to check whether Ms Tin Pei Ling used the app.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: This is part of the service delivery approach that Minister Chan Chun Sing described just now.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: After my appeal and Mrs Josephine Teo's appeal, Ms Tin Pei Ling should have the next one.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: Together, we believe that these improvements will allow all of us to save time, reduce transaction costs and increase efficiency.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: Second, Smart Nation has also tried to facilitate a safer living environment.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: We are trialing a new Personal Alert Button for the elderly to call for help, especially after a fall, when they may be immobilised.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: This was brought home to me even more starkly recently when Minister Khaw Boon Wan described when he had his fall and he fractured his arm and the intense agony that immobilised him.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: And as you would have seen in his Facebook post yesterday, this is not unique to him.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: Many elderly people have faced emergencies at home alone, immobilised and they need to call for help.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: So, this is one example in trying to make a difference at a direct personal level.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: Another example, drowning detection systems have helped our lifeguards keep community swimming pools safer.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: But more important than the apps and the technology is the fact that this is an example where technology has enabled us to express our mutual care for one another.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: Third, our initiatives have helped made it easier to do business.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: We are continuing to provide more choice and better interoperability in e-payments.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: Last year, the Smart Nation and Digital Government Group (SNDGG), the Monetary Authority of Singapore (MAS) and the Infocomm Media Development Authority (IMDA) together launched the common Singapore Quick Response Code (SGQR) standard, and the Network for Electronic Transfers (NETS) has rolled out 50,000 Unified Point-of-Sales terminals across the country.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: These initiatives have helped merchants to offer greater convenience for consumers and reduced cash usage.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: In Smart Nation, we must always be data-driven.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: So, I asked and I have been informed that e-payment values have increased to more than three times that of automated teller machine (ATM) cash withdrawals.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: So, we are moving in the right direction.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: NETS was also appointed to unify the e-payment landscape at hawker centres and coffee shops.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: This will allow the consolidation of different e-payment methods and, more importantly, faster settlement for hawkers.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: So, they receive their money the next day.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: Like individuals, businesses can now send and receive payments instantly.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: The PayNow initiative has contributed to cheque usage falling to 20% of inter-bank transfer volumes.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: MyInfo Business allows up to 220,000 SMEs to open bank accounts and apply for loans easily and quickly.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: IRAS has piloted direct submission of Goods and Services Tax (GST) returns from businesses’ accounting software, enabled by National Digital Identity (APIs), and will look to extend this to all GST-registered businesses.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: The Networked Trade Platform has reduced application time for trade permits.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: It used to take several days, now it takes one hour.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: This reduces the burden of administrative processes and enables our entrepreneurs to focus on growing their businesses instead of navigating red tape.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: Mr Teo Ser Luck and Mr Vikram Nair asked about our upcoming initiatives.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: We will continue to make our digital services more accessible, more integrated.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: We will enhance the SingPass Mobile so that it can be used for secure logins to selected private sector applications as well.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: Security will, of course, remain our central preoccupation.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: Senior Minister of State Janil Puthucheary will address Ms Sylvia Lim's question on security, because without security at the core of our Smart Nation, many of these initiatives will be at risk.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: We will expand the slew of services under Moments of Life to help citizens deal with all the significant turning points in our life, birth, school, marriage, even including end-of-life matters.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: And we will empower seniors to lead more active lives.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: MOH will share more of this in their session.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: We will continue to enhance convenience in daily life.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: HDB is looking to create smarter towns so that we can optimise land, infrastructure and utilities, and allow people to engage and form communities using these digital tools.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: This will make our heartlands more liveable, efficient, sustainable and safe.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: Businesses can look forward to more digital tools to increase connectivity both within Singapore and beyond our borders.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: And those of you in business will know that the velocity of cash flow is crucial in business.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: Anyone who has tried to open a restaurant would have known it takes many applications.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: We will try to streamline all these in the process, remove duplicate applications, reduce red tape and to give approvals faster.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: We hope to expand this effort to other industries in future.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: Our goal is to integrate all these services to help firms unlock new ways of connecting with consumers and other businesses and transacting with the Government.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: SNDGG is not doing this on our own.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: We are not a Ministry but we view ourselves as a shared platform for the whole of Government.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: The Digital Government Blueprint calls for the Government to be digital to the core by 2023.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: Many agencies have, therefore, implemented or are in the process of implementing new digital initiatives in order for us to achieve this.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: Many people have told me that they enjoy the National Steps Challenge and I am especially intrigued to see so many non-techy people wearing activity trackers.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: It is not just because the Health Promotion Board (HPB) is giving it away free, but the combination of community and activity and, of course, the usual Singapore pursuit of health points and discounts helps.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: But the point is that we have used technology to make a difference and to improve health on a daily basis.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: MCCY recently launched a central volunteer management system to deepen volunteer engagement and recruitment.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: Six public agencies now use volunteer.sg to manage over 20,000 active volunteers.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: I have described a whole slew of existing and upcoming benefits to citizens from the Smart Nation.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: But I also agree with Ms Tin Pei Ling that we must continue to our citizen-centric focused and delivering services in an integrated way.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: In the coming years, with the data generated from our expanding digital infrastructure, we can expect the services to become more personalised, more tailor-made to the individual needs of citizens and be more responsive.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: When people shop online, when people engage online, especially with the private sector, expectations are raised and they expect the Government to also be able to respond in such a personalised, responsive manner.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: One way which we are going to do this is also to make better use of AI which, we believe, will greatly improve our lives and our economy.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: AI and, in particular, deep machine learning, have revolutionised the scene in recent years.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: AI has already begun to make an impact in our daily lives.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: If we just stop to think about it, the voice assistants in our handphone, the language translations, the global positioning system (GPS) optimisation, the credit card fraud alerts, all these have benefited from advances in AI just within the last two years.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: I have mentioned just now that the Government has been using AI for drowning detection in our swimming pools.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: We have also used it for SkillsFuture's fraud detection, and for local speech recognition.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: In fact, AI speech recognition has been used to augment the transcription of COS speeches this year.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: And even if you point out mistakes, you will help us improve the system.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: Mr Cedric Foo asked how Smart Nation will keep us relevant.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: AI, data analytics, robotics and automation are crucial ingredients for us to restructure of our economy.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: We need to achieve a quantum leap in productivity by creating new engines of growth.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: The Government needs to upgrade our technology stack so that we can be more responsive to citizens’ needs and to the demands of an increasingly competitive marketplace.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: We believe that Singapore has a good foundation for AI, through a multi-agency effort from SNDGG, the Ministry of Communications and Information (MCI) and our economic agencies.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: The National Research Foundation (NRF) set up AI Singapore to bring all relevant research institutions and AI startups together.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: GovTech will set up a centre of excellence in data science and AI to help other agencies deploy these AI solutions and technologies.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: For citizens, this means new and better services, whether from the Government or private sector.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: McKinsey has identified 160 use cases where AI can be used for social good.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: For example, AI can "recommend content to students based on past successes and engagement with the material" and "detect student distress early".

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: Basically, what it means is that we talk about streams and subject banding.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: But to really be able to customise that educational journey for that individual, sometimes maybe even to gamify it, will provide a more helpful educational experience for our students.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: We also foresee AI optimising urban scenarios, for instance, in optimising our traffic light networks and to predictively maintain public infrastructure.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: In other words, make sure things do not break down or to identify potential problems, before they lead to a breakdown.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: We foresee AI applications in finance, in logistics and cybersecurity.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: In fact, there are already many local companies in these and other domains.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: This is to answer Mr Teo Ser Luck.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: We hope to co-create with these companies the development of these new AI solutions.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: We want to support SMEs to adopt AI and to work with the Government on relevant use cases.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: We will expand Government and private sector collaboration.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: This programme will also bring AI apprentices to co-train with industry.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: So, in other words, we are linking businesses to main experts and people who want to learn and enter this industry.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: Before that sounds too scary, I want to say that we do not expect everyone to become an AI expert.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: But think of AI in the future in the same way which you think of word processing today.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: It is a general-purpose technology, and we want our workforce to be able to use AI tools to participate meaningfully in the future AI-driven economy to secure good jobs, improve productivity and raise wages.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: So, let me conclude by restating the obvious.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: Smart Nation is ultimately about improving lives and livelihoods.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: Still, we cannot be complacent because the pace of technological change is so unrelentingly quick.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: And I share Ms Rahayu Mahzam's concerns on digital readiness and inclusion, and Senior Minister of State Janil Puthucheary will elaborate on the special inclusion initiatives that we will embark on to make sure no citizen is left behind.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: But these challenges and all these disruptions also bring many opportunities for Singapore, especially a city-state with hardworking, disciplined, highly educated people.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: We have disproportionate opportunities in such a world.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: We call on citizens and businesses to journey with us, to fully exploit our comparative advantage, take advantage of the resources and the infrastructure that we have put in place, and to co-create solutions for the future.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: If we do this, Mr Chairman, we can all reap the benefits of our Smart Nation for years and decades to come.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information and Transport (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: Mr Chairman, if I may follow on from Minister Vivian Balakrishnan's rallying cry for all of us to become involved in Singapore's Smart Nation ambition.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information and Transport (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: The Government cannot make this happen alone, cannot make this happen through force of will, by wishing it, by making speeches.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information and Transport (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: We need the ideas and capabilities of our people and our businesses.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information and Transport (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: As a nation, everyone needs to be part of our Smart Nation journey.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information and Transport (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: We do not have a monopoly on the best ideas and talent.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information and Transport (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: We will need to create opportunities for citizens, community partners and businesses to contribute meaningfully to Smart Nation.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information and Transport (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: Members Mr Teo Ser Luck and Mr Vikram Nair have asked about partnerships between the Government, businesses and the tech community.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information and Transport (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: This can be used to build applications and digital services.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information and Transport (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: CODEX will be modular, interoperable and will, in future, allow an interface to parties outside the Government.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information and Transport (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: As part of CODEX, we are working with public agencies to shift their ICT systems towards the commercial cloud.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information and Transport (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: So, Government, systems, public agency systems on the commercial cloud, and this will allow us to benefit from leading edge private sector capabilities to build products and services better for our citizens.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information and Transport (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: We are also actively involving the tech community.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information and Transport (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: One example is a mobile application called “Kill The Queue”, which allows shoppers to save time by scanning and paying for items through their mobile phones as they shop.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information and Transport (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: The app was conceptualised by a team of GovTech engineers.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information and Transport (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: They then partnered students from Temasek Polytechnic to build a prototype, as part of the students' final year project.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information and Transport (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: This partnership also allows students to improve their skills through solving real-world challenges.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information and Transport (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: So, partnerships through businesses by looking at how Government build platforms and products can be interoperable and can create opportunities for businesses to interface with ideas that we can seed out into the students and the academic community so that they can run with and try to develop real-world solutions.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information and Transport (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: Members may have heard of "Developers Conferences" or DevCons.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information and Transport (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: These are usually organised by tech companies, such as Apple, Google or Facebook, and they are done to engage engineers and the tech business communities to leverage upon the product or the platform owned by that company.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information and Transport (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: So, we might have an Apple on iPhone operating system (iOS) Developers Conference, for example, or Facebook Developers Conference, where the time is given for software developers and businesses to think how they can utilise that product better for their own business purposes and how their feedback then improves the product of the person running the Developers Conference.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information and Transport (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: So, what is the difference between a Developers Conference and a hackathon?

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information and Transport (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: A Developers Conference, the person organising it has a product, has a solution, has a platform and wants to ask the community how to do things better using this product, how to make the product better for you.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information and Transport (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: In a hackathon, the participants are generating ideas to solve the problems that they are concerned about and the Government also supports this.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information and Transport (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: We are extending our outreach efforts beyond the tech community because we need a Smart Nation which benefits all citizens from all walks of life.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information and Transport (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: We are actively engaging citizens on Smart Nation initiatives through a project called Smart Nation Co-Creating with our People Everywhere (SCOPE).

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information and Transport (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: SCOPE is a platform for us to bring out early prototypes of our digital products or ideas to citizens.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information and Transport (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: So, one example that Minister Vivian Balakrishnan quoted was the alert button.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information and Transport (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: Very earlier on in its design phase and its conceptualisation phase, just as soon as we have something physical, we encourage participants to play with these products, to try them out, to test them and their feedback then is used to improve our product development process.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information and Transport (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: This is something very common in the private sector.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information and Transport (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: We have collected many useful insights and suggestions.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information and Transport (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: One example of these insights is how receptive seniors are to active ageing services within the Moments of Life application.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information and Transport (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: They also gave feedback about how to design the application in an easy-to-use manner, and how to provide support and coaching to seniors so that they can use these apps and benefit from these services.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information and Transport (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: All of this will help us to develop and deliver a better product, better services and better experience.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information and Transport (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: We will continue to scale up these efforts.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information and Transport (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: I will speak more about these broader Digital Readiness efforts in the MCI COS.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information and Transport (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: But SNDGG will play our part by ensuring that the Government's digital services are designed to benefit all.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information and Transport (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: For example, HDB's website MyNiceHome is a portal that provides first-time home owners with useful information about buying and renovating a flat and this has been completely redesigned.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information and Transport (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: The site was made mobile-responsive, different forms of search and assistance had been added, and the content had been made accessible to people with disabilities.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information and Transport (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: And as a result, the site traffic has increased significantly.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information and Transport (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: Ms Sylvia Lim has asked about data protection within the public sector.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information and Transport (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: The Government should, indeed, be held to high standards for the protection of the data it collects.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information and Transport (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: In SNDGG, our role is not just about delivering good products, but also in setting and maintaining high standards of data protection for the public sector.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information and Transport (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: We have also increased the number and types of internal IT audits to check on agencies’ data access and data protection measures.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information and Transport (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: As a matter of practice, agencies will use identifiable data only when necessary, such as for providing personalised services.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information and Transport (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: We will continuously review our standards and measures and incorporate lessons learnt and industry best practices.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information and Transport (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: For example, we will be progressively automating user account management to ensure tight and robust access control.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information and Transport (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: Where citizens suspect that their data have been misused or hacked, they can lodge a complaint with the agency and, if there is any suspicion of a crime, they can make a report to the Police.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information and Transport (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: We have guidelines for the handling of data and protocols that should be in place.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information and Transport (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: Complaints will be thoroughly investigated and appropriate action taken.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information and Transport (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: On top of that, there are other issues and consequences as a result of that, and we would like to discuss the ways we can help and support them.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information and Transport (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: To build our Smart Nation platforms and products, to engage the tech community and businesses, to develop and enforce rigorous standards across the public sector, and to create jobs and opportunities for Singaporeans, we will need to build up a strong core of engineering skills.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information and Transport (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: We have been searching for engineering talent to join us.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information and Transport (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: We are looking for people with bright minds, an eye for computational design and the drive to contribute to society.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information and Transport (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: There are exciting opportunities for engineers in the Government.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information and Transport (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: And I would like to cite a particular example, Ms Laura Lee.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information and Transport (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: Members may or may not be familiar with Ms Lee's first employer King.com which is a software developer.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information and Transport (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: I suspect some Members may be more familiar with one of their products which is Candy Crush.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information and Transport (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: While Ms Lee was working at King.com, helping Candy Crush to become one of the bestselling games of all time, she read about how data was used by GovTech engineers to resolve the spate of mysterious disruptions to the Circle Line in 2016.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information and Transport (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: So, reading about that effort by our data scientists to solve these real-world problems, Ms Lee was inspired to come back home to Singapore and join us.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information and Transport (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: And now she is currently a Data Scientist with GovTech working to improve the Government’s digital services, such as transport route planning and jobs matching.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information and Transport (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: Like many of our engineers, she also pursues other projects as part of her personal professional development within the team.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information and Transport (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: Currently, she is part of a team that is trying to find ways to use technology, machine learning and our Smart Nation platforms to encourage more recycling.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information and Transport (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: This is something that she initiated as part of a hackathon she participated in, using her skills to pursue something that matters to her.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information and Transport (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: Ms Lee did not graduate with a computer science degree.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information and Transport (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: Her training was in Mathematics, Economics and Statistics.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information and Transport (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: We are hoping to make them as widespread as possible, including the jobs that are created.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information and Transport (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: It is not just for those students who are currently pursuing a Computer Science course or participating in Robotics as a co-curricular activity (CCA).

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information and Transport (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: What is important is to have the drive, curiosity and willingness to pick up new skills throughout our lives.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
text: In response, the Prime Minister replied that on the completeness of the report and the minutes, "I leave that to the Committee".

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
text: Even though the Prime Minister said that he was not in favour of publishing every twist and turn that would be reflected in the minutes, the Prime Minister was noncommittal on the prospect of a more complete report.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
